title: The ark in full
hookLine: Nuh builds, the waters come, and the ark sails in Allah's name (11:37–41)
carry: in his name it sails and anchors

lines: A WEEK: FEAR, TOO LATE, IN TIME.
cards: This week opened Block B: the friends of God, with no fear and no grief; Pharaoh's right words too late, and a whole town's just in time; the question, would you compel them; and why Hud turned the Prophet's hair gray.
Now Hud's first long story. Last year you watched Nuh build on dry land while the neighbors laughed, and call to his son on the mountain.
Today, the voyage itself, start to finish, because Surah Hud gives it a shape, and a single line people still say when they set out.

teach.b: It begins with a command, in verse thirty-seven: build the ship under Our eyes and by Our inspiration. Bi-a'yunina: under Our eyes. Every plank laid while being watched over.
Then the sign comes, water gushing out, and the order: load on it a pair of every kind, your household, and those who believe.

teach.h: AND THEY WERE ONLY A FEW.
teach.b: And the verse adds, almost quietly: and they were only a few.

teach.h: IN GOD'S NAME, ITS COURSE AND MOORING.
teach.b: Then Nuh speaks, in Pickthall's translation: "Embark therein! In the name of Allah be its course and its mooring." Bismillahi majraha wa mursaha.

Majra is the sailing, the running of the ship; mursa is the anchoring, the coming to rest. Both in God's name: the going and the stopping. Some Muslims still say these words when they board a boat or set out on a journey.
The middle of the voyage is the hard part: waves like mountains, and the son who would not come aboard. Then the ending, in verse forty-four, in a run of short commands.
Earth, swallow your water. Sky, hold back. The water sinks away, the command is fulfilled, the ship comes to rest on al-Judi.
And in verse forty-eight, the last word to Nuh: go down, in peace from Us, and with blessings on you and on the peoples who will come from those with you. Read in full, the voyage has three parts.

teach.h: IN HIS NAME IT SAILS AND ANCHORS.
teach.b: It sets out in God's name. It comes to rest in God's name. And it steps off in peace.

how: Some Muslims recite Nuh's words from 11:41, bismillahi majraha wa mursaha, when boarding a ship or setting out on a journey, alongside the traveler's supplication taught in the hadith.

games.q: the ship is built, the water is coming, and the believers stand at the ramp. you're Nuh. what do you say?
o: embark: in God's name its course and its mooring.
each of you, find your own place.
games.why: embark therein! in the name of Allah be its course and its mooring (11:41): the going and the stopping, both in God's name.

practice: Think of the next journey you'll take, even a small one, the drive to work or the walk to the store, and picture the moment you set off and the moment you arrive.
If you pray, you can say Nuh's words at both ends: in God's name its course, in God's name its mooring. If not, simply give the start and the stop a breath of attention.
